Calculate All Available Silhouette Summaries

Source: R/calSilhouette.R
calSilhouette.Rd

Computes every silhouette width available in the package for one clustering and returns a data frame comparing the crisp, fuzzy, and median averages of each.

Usage

calSilhouette(
  prox_matrix = NULL,
  proximity_type = c("dissimilarity", "similarity"),
  prob_matrix = NULL,
  a = 2,
  print.summary = FALSE,
  clust_fun = NULL,
  ...,
  cluster = NULL,
  clust_args = list()
)

Arguments

prox_matrix

A numeric matrix where rows represent observations and columns represent proximity measures (e.g., distances or similarities) to clusters. Typically, this is a membership or dissimilarity matrix from clustering results. If clust_fun is provided, prox_matrix should be the name of the matrix component as a string (e.g., if clust_fun = fcm from ppclust package the prox_matrix = "d"). Defaults to NULL.

proximity_type

Character string specifying the type of proximity measure in prox_matrix. Options are "similarity" (higher values indicate closer proximity) or "dissimilarity" (lower values indicate closer proximity). Defaults to "dissimilarity".

prob_matrix

A numeric matrix of cluster membership probabilities, where rows represent observations and columns represent clusters in the same order as prox_matrix. If clust_fun is provided, prob_matrix can be given as the name of the matrix component (e.g., "u" for the fcm function). Defaults to NULL.

a

Non-negative number, the exponent \(\alpha\) of the weights in fuzzy silhouette averaging. Higher values increase the emphasis on strong membership differences; a = 0 gives every observation the same weight, so the fuzzy average equals the crisp average. Defaults to 2.

print.summary

Logical; if TRUE, reports the summary table through message. Defaults to FALSE.

clust_fun

Optional S3 or S4 function object or function as character string specifying a clustering function that produces the proximity measure matrix. For example, fcm or "fcm". If provided, prox_matrix must be the name of the matrix component in the clustering output (e.g., "d" for fcm when proximity_type = "dissimilarity"). Defaults to NULL.

...

Additional arguments passed to clust_fun, such as x,centers for fcm.

cluster

Optional integer vector of length \(n\) giving the cluster of each observation as a column number (\(1, \ldots, K\)). If clust_fun is provided, cluster may be the name of the label component of its output. Must be named in the call because it follows .... See Cluster labels.

clust_args

A list of further arguments for clust_fun. Arguments given through ... are matched first against this function's own arguments, and R matches names partially: m = 3 meant for the fuzzifier of fcm would be taken as method. Pass such arguments here instead, e.g. clust_args = list(m = 3). Defaults to list().

Value

A data frame with one row per method and the following columns:

Method

Character vector of method names, as listed in Details.

Crisp

Crisp (unweighted mean) average silhouette width.

Fuzzy

Fuzzy (membership-weighted) average silhouette width; present only when prob_matrix is supplied.

Median

Median silhouette width.

Details

The rows are not independent pieces of evidence: several are exact or monotone transformations of one another (see Relations between the rows). The distance-based rows compare distances to the cluster representatives; the probability-based rows are the silhouettes of Bhat Kapu and Kiruthika (2024), which treat the posterior probabilities or the component densities as proximities, and the density-based silhouette of Menardi (2011).

The methods included depend on the available input matrices:

If prox_matrix is available:

  • medoid - Medoid-based silhouette using Silhouette

  • pac - PAC-based silhouette using Silhouette

If prob_matrix is available:

  • pp_pac - PACS: posterior probabilities with the PAC normalization (softSilhouette)

  • pp_medoid - PPS: posterior probability silhouette (softSilhouette)

  • nlpp_pac - Negative log posterior probabilities with the PAC normalization (softSilhouette)

  • nlpp_medoid - NLPPS: negative log of posterior probability silhouette (softSilhouette)

  • pd_pac - Probability densities with the PAC normalization (softSilhouette)

  • pd_medoid - PDS: probability density silhouette (softSilhouette)

  • cer - CeS: certainty silhouette (cerSilhouette)

  • db - DBS: density-based silhouette of Menardi (2011) (dbSilhouette)

At least one of prox_matrix or prob_matrix must be provided. Each width is computed once and summarized by all available averages; the fuzzy average needs prob_matrix.

If a width cannot be computed, its row is NA and a warning gives the reason. Warnings from the individual functions are collected and each distinct warning is reported once.

Cluster labels

When cluster is supplied, every row scores that partition. Otherwise every row except the PDS rows (pd_pac, pd_medoid) uses the largest membership in prob_matrix, or the closest cluster in prox_matrix when there are no memberships. The PDS rows assign each observation to its largest density, as in the definition of the PDS (see softSilhouette); this agrees with the largest membership when the clusters have equal estimated weights. (In version 0.9.6 and earlier, the crisp and median distance-based rows used the closest cluster in prox_matrix even when prob_matrix was supplied.)

Relations between the rows

For the same labels, the rows fall into the following groups.

Monotone transformations of each other (same ranking of observations).

Each pac width is \(s/(2 - |s|)\) of the corresponding medoid width \(s\): medoid/pac, pp_medoid/pp_pac, nlpp_medoid/nlpp_pac and pd_medoid/pd_pac. With the default labels, pp_medoid, pp_pac and db are all increasing functions of the ratio of the two largest memberships, so they too rank observations identically. The averages still differ, and may peak at different numbers of clusters.

Equal in special cases.

pd (PDS) equals pp (PPS) when all estimated cluster weights are equal. For fuzzy c-means with fuzzifier \(m\), pp_medoid and pp_pac equal medoid and pac computed from the dissimilarities \(d_{ik}^{1/(m-1)}\), where \(d_{ik}\) are squared Euclidean distances to the prototypes (for \(m = 2\), the d component of fcm).

Genuinely different.

The distance-based rows (in general), nlpp (which also depends on the size of the neighboring membership), and cer (the largest membership alone, bounded below by \(1/K\)).

Choosing the number of clusters

Computing calSilhouette() over \(k = 2, 3, \ldots\) gives one curve per row. The distance-based rows are usually read at their maximum. Bhat Kapu and Kiruthika (2024) read the probability-based rows from the reverse elbow drop of the curve, and the DBS from its local maxima (Menardi, 2011). The suggested number of clusters depends on the algorithm that produced the memberships, on the width and on the averaging.

References

Bhat Kapu, S., & Kiruthika. (2024). Some density-based silhouette diagnostics for soft clustering algorithms. Communications in Statistics: Case Studies, Data Analysis and Applications, 10(3-4), 221-238. doi:10.1080/23737484.2024.2408534

Menardi, G. (2011). Density-based silhouette diagnostics for clustering methods. Statistics and Computing, 21(3), 295–308. doi:10.1007/s11222-010-9169-0

See also

Silhouette, softSilhouette, dbSilhouette, cerSilhouette

Examples

if (requireNamespace("ppclust", quietly = TRUE)) {
  # Example with FCM clustering
  library(ppclust)
  data(iris)
  fcm_result <- fcm(iris[, -5], centers = 3)

  # Using matrices directly
  summary_result <- calSilhouette(
    prox_matrix = fcm_result$d,
    prob_matrix = fcm_result$u,
    proximity_type = "dissimilarity",
    print.summary = TRUE
  )
}
#> Summary of All Silhouette Methods
#> ==========================================
#>       Method     Crisp     Fuzzy    Median
#>       medoid 0.8288288 0.9297577 0.9179945
#>          pac 0.7541271 0.8799106 0.8484197
#>       pp_pac 0.7541271 0.8799106 0.8484197
#>    pp_medoid 0.8288288 0.9297577 0.9179945
#>     nlpp_pac 0.8185224 0.9304926 0.9261387
#>  nlpp_medoid 0.8749545 0.9604788 0.9616532
#>       pd_pac 0.7469894 0.8784604 0.8562152
#>    pd_medoid 0.8196600 0.9279118 0.9225377
#>          cer 0.8572481 0.9248327 0.9041529
#>           db 0.3303585 0.4206051 0.3097745

if (requireNamespace("ppclust", quietly = TRUE)) {
  # Using clustering function
  summary_result2 <- calSilhouette(
    prox_matrix = "d",
    prob_matrix = "u",
    proximity_type = "dissimilarity",
    clust_fun = ppclust::fcm,
    x = iris[, -5],
    centers = 3,
    print.summary = TRUE
  )
}
